question: Every term we retrain our placement model on how students did in the level it gave them, so its own placements become part of its next training data. Does the AI Act say anything about this?
gold_source: Article 15(4), third subparagraph; Article 10(2), points (f) and (g)
gold_answer: For a high-risk AI system, Article 15(4), third subparagraph, requires high-risk AI systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market or put into service to be developed in such a way as to eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of possibly biased outputs influencing input for future operations (feedback loops), and as to ensure that any such feedback loops are duly addressed with appropriate mitigation measures. For the data, Article 10(2) requires training, validation and testing data sets to be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose; these practices concern in particular the examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where data outputs influence inputs for future operations (point (f)), and appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f) (point (g)). The answer does not decide whether the tool is high-risk.

question: I'm on the compliance team. Under the current consolidated text, when may the provider of a high-risk level placement system process special categories of personal data to detect and correct bias in its model?
gold_answer: Under Article 4a(1), to the extent strictly necessary to ensure bias detection and correction in relation to high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 10(2), points (f) and (g), providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons. In addition to Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable, all of the following conditions must be met: (a) the bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data; (b) the special categories of personal data are subject to technical limitations on the re-use of personal data, and state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation; (c) they are subject to measures to ensure that the personal data processed are secured and protected, subject to suitable safeguards, including strict controls and documentation of the access, to avoid misuse and to ensure that only authorised persons have access to those personal data with appropriate confidentiality obligations; (d) they are not transmitted, transferred or otherwise accessed by other parties; (e) they are deleted once the bias has been corrected or the personal data has reached the end of its retention period, whichever comes first; and (f) the records of processing activities include the reasons why the processing was strictly necessary to detect and correct biases, and why that objective could not be achieved by processing other data. This is the rule of the consolidated text of 27/07/2026; Article 4a(1) comes from Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

question: Our placement engine has no trained model: it uses scoring rules and cut-off points that our teachers wrote. If it still counts as a high-risk AI system, which of the AI Act's data set requirements apply to it?
gold_answer: Article 10(1) concerns high-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data: they must be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria of paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of Article 10 and of Article 4a(1) whenever such data sets are used. Under Article 10(6), for the development of high-risk AI systems not using techniques involving the training of AI models, paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of Article 10 and Article 4a(1) apply only to the testing data sets. For such a system, the testing data sets must be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose of the system, which concern in particular the points listed in Article 10(2), among them data collection processes and the origin of data, relevant data-preparation processing operations, an assessment of the availability, quantity and suitability of the data sets that are needed, and the examination of possible biases and appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate them; they must be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose, with the appropriate statistical properties (Article 10(3)); and they must take into account, to the extent required by the intended purpose, the characteristics or elements that are particular to the specific geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting within which the system is intended to be used (Article 10(4)). The answer does not decide whether the engine is an AI system or whether it is high-risk.

question: I'm building the teacher screen of our placement tool, which language schools will run. Does every human oversight measure have to be built into our software, or can some be left for the schools to put in place?
gold_answer: Article 14(1) requires high-risk AI systems to be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use. Under Article 14(3), the oversight measures must be commensurate with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use of the high-risk AI system, and are ensured through either one or both of two types of measures: (a) measures identified and built, when technically feasible, into the high-risk AI system by the provider before it is placed on the market or put into service; (b) measures identified by the provider before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service and that are appropriate to be implemented by the deployer. So not every measure has to be built into the system, but in both cases the provider identifies the measures before the system is placed on the market or put into service. The provisions do not say which specific measures belong to each type, and the answer does not decide whether the tool is high-risk.

question: Before launch we have to test our placement model. What probability threshold, for example 0.8, does the AI Act require before a student is placed in a level?
gold_answer: Expected behaviour: abstain. Article 9(8) requires the testing of high-risk AI systems to be performed, as appropriate, at any time throughout the development process, and, in any event, prior to their being placed on the market or put into service, against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system. The in-scope provisions do not give a value for such a threshold. The answer says this in one sentence and gives no number.
